title: Master Class | French Defense | Chess Speedrun | Grandmaster Naroditsky
openingName: French Defense: Advance Variation vs 3...b6 (...Ba6 plan)

moves.spoken: The French, and against it the pawn to e5 — the Advance. The clamp goes up and Black must find counterplay against it.
moves.teaches: e5 is the thematic Advance clamp against the French.

moves.spoken: Instead of the main move c5, Black tries the pawn to b6 — an old sideline. The whole idea is the bishop to a6, to swap off the light-squared bishop that the French normally leaves boxed in behind e6.
moves.teaches: Against the Advance, ...b6 aims to trade Black's bad light-squared bishop via ...Ba6.
moves.plans: Prevent or punish the bishop trade.

moves.spoken: The pawn to c3 quietly does two jobs. It props up d4 — and it clears the d1-a4 diagonal, so that if the bishop comes to a6, White captures and then the queen to a4 checks the king while forking the knight on a6.
moves.teaches: c3 opens the d1-a4 diagonal: ...Ba6 Bxa6 Nxa6 Qa4+ forks king and knight.
moves.plans: c3, then meet ...Ba6 with the Qa4+ fork.

moves.spoken: With the bishop trade defused, just develop nicely — the bishop to d3, taking a good diagonal and preparing to castle.
moves.teaches: Once the opponent's key idea is stopped, develop by principle.

moves.spoken: The knight goes to e2, not f3 — deliberately. Keeping the f-pawn free lets it charge f4 and f5 later, and that pawn on e6 is exactly the target the storm will crash into.
moves.teaches: Develop the knight to e2 to keep the f-pawn free for the f4-f5 break against e6.

moves.spoken: Don't rush the f-pawn — castle and complete the setup first. Black is grabbing queenside space instead of developing, which is the signal to finish preparing and then hit the gas with f4.
moves.teaches: Complete development before launching the pawn storm; punish an undeveloping opponent by speeding up.

moves.spoken: This is the recurring theme against the French: Black always wants to get rid of that light-squared bishop. The bishop to a6 is the try — and move order decides whether it's punished.
moves.teaches: Recognise Black's standing wish to trade the bad French bishop and time your response.
moves.plans: Trade on a6 at the right moment.

moves.spoken: The wrong order: the immediate queen to a4 check runs into the queen to d7, blocking and hitting back — there's no time to grab the bishop, and after the king recaptures Black is out of the woods. You must trade on a6 first, then win the knight.
moves.teaches: Move order matters: capture the bishop first, then Qa4+ wins the knight — the check first fails to ...Qd7.

moves.spoken: Black keeps neglecting development, so castle and bang on the gas — the pawn to f4. Against the knight to h6, the quiet h3 keeps things in hand before committing the storm; the natural-looking knight to g3 has a hidden drawback here.
moves.teaches: Speed up against a lagging opponent, but check for the tactical drawback before the obvious preparing move.
